audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3..6].side all read Skill while win[3..6] read Zoe, Anivia, Anivia, Anivia; the packet chart agrees with win[].
audit.why: Four rows rendering two different answers to who wins the stage.

Level 6 is the flip for Anivia. Zoe's own 6 is not a power spike in the usual sense — Portal Jump is an 11s 575-range blink out and back, so it raises her safety, not her damage; her damage spike is Sleepy Trouble Bubble rank-ups and AP.
audit.corrected: Stated the blink's real cooldown and behaviour in breakdown.cooldowns and whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors: the poke is called a 'Q-W combo' (W is Spell Thief, which only re-casts summoner spell remnants — it is not poke she can throw at will), 'her passive lets her proc extra damage on immobile targets like you' (More Sparkles! is bonus damage on her next basic attack after any cast, nothing to do with immobility), and the bubble's actual mechanics are never stated.
audit.why: Riot text: Paddle Star is a redirectable missile that 'deals more damage the longer it flies in a straight line'; Sleepy Trouble Bubble makes the target drowsy then asleep, reduces their Magic Resist, and the first source of damage that breaks the sleep is doubled.
audit.corrected: Poke is Paddle Star and it punishes distance, so you walk toward it rather than away. Bubble strips MR and doubles the wake-up hit. Sidestepping early is bad because she can re-aim mid-flight.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere (sequencingCues 0), and no Zoe ability was ever named.
audit.why: Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18s at rank 1 is her only CC; Portal Jump 11s at rank 1 is the escape. Those two timers decide every step-up.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with both numbers; Paddle Star, Spell Thief, Sleepy Trouble Bubble, Portal Jump and More Sparkles! now appear by name.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing lists Sleepy Trouble Bubble under 'bypasses stacking resistances' and the kit flags trueDamage on it.
audit.why: Riot's text says the bubble REDUCES the sleeping target's Magic Resist and doubles the first damage source — there is no true damage component. The trueDamage flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire, but the MR shred makes the practical advice the same.
audit.corrected: Wrote the MR reduction, not true damage.

edits.before: Zoe's Q-W poke combo, especially when thrown from bush range, does more damage than anything you can answer with at levels 1-2, and if she lands sleepy bubble you're looking at a full burst combo before Wall is even up. More Sparkles! adds bonus damage to her next auto after every cast, which makes early trades extremely dangerous, so you need to play from max range, respect bush vision, and avoid overextending for CS.

notes: Zoe was referred to as 'he' in the tldr and its report mirror; fixed in the same pass as the mechanical corrections there. Spell Thief is not poke she can throw at will — it only re-casts summoner spell remnants — so every 'Q-W combo' reference misdescribed the lane. More Sparkles! is an on-cast empowered auto, not an anti-immobile proc. The single most actionable fact the page was missing: Paddle Star scales with flight distance and is redirectable, so you walk INTO it and dodge late. Left tradeGood/tradeBad and the phases[N].why lines alone — still templated but I had nothing Zoe-specific to ground them in beyond what the fields above now carry; flagging them rather than inventing.
